discovered-from:AH-0MUZDXF2U001MJW1

## Problem

Running `npm run build` from a git worktree created by the implement skill fails at the `build-audio` step:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'tsx' imported from /home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/node_modules/toneforge/bin/dev-cli.js
```

## Root cause

`scripts/build-audio.mjs` `resolveToneForge()` resolves the sibling checkout as `join(repoRoot, '..', 'ToneForge')`. Inside a worktree (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`) that path is `.worklog/worktrees/ToneForge`, which does not exist, so resolution falls through to `tf` on PATH (`node_modules/.bin/tf -> ../toneforge/bin/dev-cli.js`). That copy has no `tsx` dependency, so the CLI crashes.

When built from the main checkout the sibling path resolves correctly and the build succeeds.

## Workaround used

`TONEFORGE_CLI=/home/rgardler/projects/ToneForge/bin/dev-cli.js npm run build` (the sibling's `node_modules` has `tsx`).

## Expected behaviour

`npm run build` succeeds inside a worktree without requiring `TONEFORGE_CLI` to be set manually, since worktrees are the mandated implementation workflow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `npm run build` succeeds from a worktree with no `TONEFORGE_CLI` set.
- AC2: Sibling resolution is anchored to the main checkout (e.g. via the git common dir) rather than the worktree root.
- AC3: Existing `build-audio` tests still pass and the main-checkout build is unaffected.
data.title: build-audio sibling ToneForge resolution fails inside git worktrees

data.description:
## Seed intent (operator report)

> A recent change has made later levels/wave enemies to circle around the player. I don't like it. Identify what it is and explain what the intent. It may be interesting for a specific enemy to do this, but not for all.

Priority requested by operator: **critical**.

## Initial identification (agent, pre-intake investigation)

**Symptom.** In the shipped (default) campaign, the later waves are dominated by
a single player-relative archetype so the enemies appear to circle / follow the
player rather than holding formation:

- Level 4 wave 2 is `diver x18` — the Diver unit re-anchors so the whole unit
  re-forms around the dive's attack-end (the player's position), i.e. the wave
  migrates to wherever the player is.
- Level 5 waves are `phaser x12` groups in the `orbital` formation — the Phaser
  entity orbits a centre in a fixed-radius circle, so the wave reads as a
  rotating ring.

**What actually changed.** The shipped campaign is no longer the hand-authored
`LEVELS`; since `sequencedWavesEnabled` defaults to `true`, `PlayScene` builds
the campaign from the difficulty-curve config via `buildSequencedLevels()` ->
`difficultySequencer.sequencer()`. The sequencer picks each wave's composition by
minimising error against a difficulty target using `enemyDifficulty`, whose
`formationKind` ordinal ranks `orbital` hardest (5) and whose Phaser archetype
scores highest overall. There is **no composition / variety constraint**, so the
high later-level targets (L5W1 = 43.5, L5W2 = 62) collapse onto Phaser (orbital)
groups, and the pool also admits special spawner-delivered archetypes
(`boss`, `lane-traffic`, `march`) as wave filler.

**Intent of the affected behaviour.** The Phaser's fixed orbital path is a
deliberate, documented archetype design (E4 Phaser, GDD 4.1 / Level 5
"Predictable Death": a memorisable late-game pattern). The auto-sequencer was
introduced (AH-0MUITS0VD000DVSV) purely to auto-generate a difficulty curve
without hand-authoring every wave. Neither was intended to make *every*
later-level enemy circle/follow the player.

## Open question for the operator

Which observation is the one you saw? (Phaser ring in L5 / Diver unit following
the player in L4 / both / a different enemy I should look at.)
data.title: Later-level waves collapse to circling (orbital/player-following) enemies — auto-sequencer composition
